Alex W: Heads up — customer running a private on‑prem deployment reported cross-tenant ACL hits after we rolled the RBAC templates. Seen in EMEA cluster. P1?
Maria G: Can you paste the alert/log lines? which tenant affected? :eyes:
Alex W: Alert snippet below (sanitized):
```
2026-03-05T12:34:11Z WARN auth: allowed access to /models.list for tenant=tenant-b via sa=svc-cfgsync
src=api-gateway pod=api-gw-4
KMSKeyID=proj-eu-01/key-abc-123
```
sec-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-487 (severity=P1) — ticket linked.
Jordan K: My guess: config-sync mapping change. We pushed config-sync v2 to private clusters last night which changed the SA->role mapping.
Samir P: Confirmed — we rolled v2.0.1 to 3 on‑prem clusters at ~2165429000. It included the new serviceAccount mapping patch.
Leah T: If SA mapping was too permissive, it could let svc-cfgsync act across namespaces. Immediate containment: revoke SA tokens, apply restrictive NetworkPolicy to deny egress to cross-tenant endpoints, and force KMS CMK rotation for affected key.
Alex W: Doing containment now: revoked tokens for svc-cfgsync, applied a quick deny-egress policy. Patch we applied:
```
kubectl -n infra patch serviceaccount svc-cfgsync -p '{"metadata": {"annotations": {"redwood.io/revoked": "true"}}}'
kubectl -n infra delete secret $(kubectl -n infra get secret | grep svc-cfgsync | awk '{print $1}')
```
And NetworkPolicy:
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-cross-tenant-egress
  namespace: infra
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cfgsync
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress: []
```
Maria G: Quick KMS question — if we rotate the customer CMK, will we break existing volume keys or model artifacts that are wrapped? Need to know rewrap capability before rotating. @Jordan K?
Jordan K: Our KMS integration supports envelope rewrap: kms.rewrap() will re-encrypt DEKs with the new CMK id. Safe flow: snapshot metadata -> rewrap DEKs -> update annotations -> rotate. We'll need to run this during a maintenance window. I'll prepare the script.
Samir P: Triage note: config-sync v2 included an updated 3rd‑party lib (yaml-parser) with CVE-2025-9999 fixed in v2.0.1. Possible exploit window between 2165400000 and 2165429000. We're scanning images for pods that ran the vulnerable binary.
Leah T: Action items for IR and post-incident controls:
- Confirm blast radius (which tenants/namespaces accessed)
- Preserve audit logs and kube-apiserver request logs for 90 days (policy).
- Push immutable copy of affected audit logs to customer-backed objectstore (or WORM store for on‑prem).
- Add admission controller that enforces netpol + default RBAC hardening on private deployments.
Alex W: For on‑prem airgapped installs where S3 isn't available, propose a local WORM object store + periodic remote aggregator (pull model) to central REDWOOD SOC. I'll draft runbook.
Maria G: I'll open the postmortem and assign owners. Quick wins: revert config-sync mapping change, add unit test for SA->role mapping, add a KMS rotation runbook for private deployments.
Jordan K: Starting the rewrap dry-run in 30m (will do on a snapshot, not live keys). I'll post progress.
Samir P: Scanning images now, will flag any pod that executed cfgsync binary between the window.
Alex W: Thanks all — keep updates in this thread. If anyone needs escalations to SRE or legal for customer notification, ping me. :thumbsup:
